title: Alternative routes in
summary: Off-cycle, boutiques, Big Four, and the lateral path — how each one actually works.

blocks.md: The front door is the summer analyst programme at a bulge bracket. There are at least four side doors, and analyst classes are full of people who used them.

**1. Off-cycle internships** (3–6 months, rolling). European banks and elite boutiques hire off-cycle continuously and screen more on availability and technicals than on university. A placement year makes you eligible; so does a January–June gap after graduating. Apply from September for January starts.

**2. Regional and mid-market boutiques**. Smaller teams, real deal exposure, and hiring managers who read every CV themselves. Twelve months at a boutique plus a strong technical interview is a well-trodden lateral into a bulge bracket at analyst 1–2.

**3. Big Four → banking**. Transaction Services, Valuations or Corporate Finance at a Big Four firm hires on a much broader university list. Two years plus an ACA gets interviews at mid-market and some bulge-bracket M&A teams.

**4. Adjacent seats**. Equity research, DCM/ECM syndicate, corporate development at a listed company, or a Big Four audit seat on a bank client. Each one gives you a story and a network that makes the next application a lateral rather than a graduate one.

**Choosing**

Rank by *probability × how much the seat teaches you*, not by brand. An off-cycle at a bank you have never heard of that puts you on two live deals beats an insight day at a name everyone knows.
